
## Introduction

```{r}
#| include: false
root <- here::here()
TR_LABEL <- paste(prettyNum(TR_gmdp, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE), collapse = ", ")
Hs_range <- range(as.numeric(sub("^S", "", IDg_gmdp)))
n_IDg    <- length(IDg_gmdp)
n_IDm    <- length(IDm_gmdp)
n_TR     <- length(TR_gmdp)
n_Da     <- length(Da_gmdp)
n_models <- sum(Dn_weights > 0)
n_rigid    <- sum(grepl("^(YG|AM|JB|SR)", names(Dn_weights[Dn_weights > 0])))
n_flexible <- sum(grepl("^(BT|BM)", names(Dn_weights[Dn_weights > 0])))
```

### Background

`r params$client$name` is advancing the designs of the Quebradona copper-gold project in `r params$location`. The project includes two compacted filtered tailings storage facilities (TSFs) -- a Non-Acid Generating (NAG) TSF and a Potentially Acid Generating (PAG) TSF -- designed to store approximately 45 Mm$^3$ and 9.1 Mm$^3$, respectively, of filtered tailings over the life of mine.

As part of an integrated program of geotechnical analyses for the Quebradona TSFs, the present study (Task 500) addresses the determination of the horizontal seismic coefficient $k_h$ for pseudo-static slope stability assessment through a performance-based displacement approach, as an alternative to the prescriptive coefficients established in ANLA's Terms of Reference TDR-13 (2016).

ANLA's TDR-13 requires pseudo-static analysis under seismic conditions with $k_h = 0.50 \times \mathrm{PGA}$ and a minimum factor of safety of 1.2. ANLA Concepto Tecnico 02268 (April 2022) specifies that for the operations and closure scenario the pseudo-static coefficient must satisfy $k_h \geq 0.50 \times \mathrm{PGA}$ for the operating earthquake ($T_R > 50$ years), and for the post-closure scenario the PGA from the maximum design earthquake ($T_R \geq 475$ years) is adopted at 100%. The TDR does not preclude alternative methodologies, provided they are technically substantiated: "different methodological procedures may be used in accordance with the variables to be measured, the application of which must be duly substantiated" (Compiled TdR, Methodology Section).

The performance-based horizontal seismic coefficient $k_{\max}$ integrates site-specific PSHA with an ensemble of Newmark displacement models. The coefficient is defined as the minimum yield acceleration ratio for which the probability of exceeding a specified allowable displacement is controlled at a target exceedance level.

### Scope

The study comprises the estimation of $k_{\max}$ and the equivalent coefficient $k_h$ [%PGA] for `r params$site`, `r params$location`, across `r n_IDg` embankment geometry classes with heights from `r Hs_range[1]` to `r Hs_range[2]` m, `r n_IDm` material scenarios defined by USCS soil classifications, `r n_TR` return periods (`r TR_LABEL` years), and `r n_Da` admissible displacement thresholds.

### Objectives

**Seismic Hazard.** Computation of site-specific hazard curves, uniform hazard spectra, and peak ground acceleration values at reference-rock conditions ($v_{\mathrm{ref}}$ = `r Vref_gmdp[1]` m/s) for `r n_TR` return periods (`r TR_LABEL` years), using seismic sources and seismicity parameters from the Global Earthquake Model (GEM).

**Site Response.** Estimation of site-amplified peak ground acceleration and spectral ordinates for site conditions with $v_{s,30}$ ranging from `r min(Vs30_gmdp)` to `r max(Vs30_gmdp)` m/s, with amplification model uncertainty propagated as an independent lognormal dispersion through Monte Carlo simulation.

**Fundamental Period.** Estimation of the fundamental period $T_n$, the maximum shear modulus $G_o$, and the base shear-wave velocity $v_S^o$ for each combination of embankment geometry (`r n_IDg` classes, heights `r Hs_range[1]` to `r Hs_range[2]` m) and material scenario (`r n_IDm` USCS classifications), using the Ishihara stiffness model and the eigenvalue expression for laterally constrained embankments.

**Newmark Displacement Model.** Estimation of permanent slope displacements using an ensemble of `r n_models` Newmark models -- `r n_rigid` rigid-block and `r n_flexible` flexible-block formulations -- aggregated through an epistemic logic-tree weighting scheme. Ground-motion intensity measures are sampled from the PSHA hazard fractiles with site amplification and inter-period correlation propagated jointly through `r NS` Monte Carlo realizations per scenario.

**Seismic Coefficients.** Determination of $k_{\max}$ in pseudo-spectral acceleration units and $k_h$ in [%PGA] by inversion of the Newmark displacement framework, for each combination of return period, embankment geometry, material scenario, and admissible displacement threshold $D_a$. Tabulated values are reported for all `r n_TR` return periods, `r n_IDg` geometry classes, `r n_IDm` material scenarios, and `r n_Da` displacement thresholds.
